study.name: Setúbal
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Setúbal” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The port city on the Sado estuary, a harbour of fishing and shipping, which gave the fortified wine its name and shipped it; the vineyards lie west of it under the Arrábida.

study.name: Portalegre
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Portalegre” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The northernmost sub-region, on the granite of the Serra de São Mamede against the Spanish border, with vineyards at six to seven hundred metres and higher: cooler, wetter, picked weeks after the plain, with old mixed bush vines that give the Alentejo's freshest and most fragrant reds and whites. The exam's Alentejo exception.

study.name: Borba
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Borba” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The marble country north-east of Évora with Estremoz and Vila Viçosa, on clay and limestone with marble outcrops: firm, balanced reds from Aragonez and Trincadeira, and a co-operative founded in 1955 whose cork-labelled red is a national standard.

study.name: Estremoz
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Estremoz” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The marble town beside Borba, on the sub-region's northern edge, home to some of the plain's most serious family estates.

study.name: Redondo
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Redondo” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: South of Borba under the Serra d'Ossa, on schist and granite: ripe, generous reds, a strong co-operative and a tradition of clay talhas in the village cellars.

study.name: Vidigueira
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Vidigueira” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Below the Serra do Mendro fault, where the plain drops into the lower Alentejo: the warmest and earliest of the sub-regions but for the south-east, the home of Antão Vaz for whites, and with Vila de Frades the heartland of talha wine.

study.name: Vila de Frades
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Vila de Frades” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The village of the talhas, where clay vessels stand in the cellars and the wine is opened on Saint Martin's Day; the capital of Vinho de Talha.

study.name: Alqueva
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Alqueva” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The reservoir on the Guadiana, filled from 2002 and one of the largest artificial lakes in western Europe, which brought irrigation to the dry south-east and water to Reguengos, Moura and Granja-Amareleja.

study.name: Évora

study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Évora” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The sub-region around the Roman and university city at the centre of the province, on granite and clay: the site of the Cartuxa cellar, named for the Carthusian monastery beside it, and of the icon red named after a medieval wine of the city, Pêra-Manca.

study.name: Moura
study.match: reviewed settlement centre associated with lesson
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Moura” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The southernmost sub-region, on the Guadiana near the Alqueva dam, hot and dry on schist and limestone: full, ripe reds from Aragonez, Trincadeira and Alicante Bouschet.

study.name: Funchal
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Funchal” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The capital and port on the south coast where the lodges stand and the wine is aged, blended and shipped; the city's lofts are where canteiro happens, and the oldest stocks on the island lie in its cellars.

study.name: Câmara de Lobos
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Câmara de Lobos” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The fishing town west of Funchal and the heart of the south coast vineyard, warm and sunny: the home of Tinta Negra, Boal and Malvasia and of two of the island's producing houses, with the terraces of Estreito de Câmara de Lobos climbing behind it and, to the west under a cliff, the Fajã dos Padres with its old Malvasia Cândida vines, reached by cable car.

study.name: Estreito de Câmara de Lobos
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Estreito de Câmara de Lobos” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The parish above the town, the island's most important vine parish, where the terraces rise through the warm belt of Tinta Negra into Boal and, higher, Sercial and Verdelho.

study.name: Jardim da Serra
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Jardim da Serra” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The high parish above Estreito, cool and often in cloud, where Sercial grows at the top of its range.

study.name: Calheta
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Calheta” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The sunny south-western coast beyond Câmara de Lobos, warm enough for Malvasia and Boal low by the sea, with terraces of Tinta Negra above them.

study.name: São Vicente
study.lessonName: São Vicente and the north coast
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “São Vicente and the north coast” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Wetter, cloudier and cooler, facing the trade winds: the north-coast parishes of São Vicente, Seixal and Porto Moniz grow Verdelho and Sercial on narrow ledges above the sea, and much Tinta Negra on the lower slopes.

study.lessonNote: The upper end of the vineyards, where the valley is a rock gorge: the Eck, slate and greywacke, late ripening and tense.

study.name: Mayschoß
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Mayschoss” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Home of the cooperative founded in 1868, the oldest in Germany; the Mönchberg on steep slate above the village.

study.name: Rech
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Rech” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: A small village on a tight bend; the Herrenberg, slate and greywacke, makes firm, long lived Spätburgunder.

study.name: Dernau
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Dernau” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The upper valley's leading village: the Pfarrwingert, a terraced slate bowl, and the Hardtberg above it; the dry Burgundian turn of the 1980s began here.

study.name: Marienthal
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Marienthal” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: A former convent and later the state domaine of the Ahr; the Klostergarten and Trotzenberg on slate below the ruin.

study.name: Walporzheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Walporzheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Kräuterberg, a steep south facing wall of slate, and the Gärkammer, one of the smallest single vineyards in Germany; the valley's grandest Pinot Noir and the Bereich's name.

study.name: Ahrweiler
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Ahrweiler” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The walled medieval town where the valley opens: the Rosenthal and Silberberg on loess and loam over slate give rounder, riper, earlier Spätburgunder.

study.name: Bad Neuenahr
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Bad Neuenahr” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The spa town beside Ahrweiler; the Sonnenberg, a broad slope of loess and slate, ripe and generous.

study.name: Heimersheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Heimersheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The last village before the Rhine plain, on loess: the Landskrone and Burggarten, the warmest, softest wines of the valley.

study.name: Trittenheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Trittenheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Upstream of Piesport, the Apotheke on a sharp bend: delicate, floral Riesling.

study.name: Piesport
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Piesport” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: A horseshoe bend of slate facing due south: Goldtröpfchen, the little drop of gold, gives ripe, peachy, honeyed Riesling. The Grosslage Piesporter Michelsberg borrows the name for flat land across the river.

study.name: Graach
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Graach” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Between Bernkastel and Wehlen: Himmelreich, broad and reliable, and Domprobst, steeper and deeper with more loam; firmer wines than Wehlen's.

study.name: Ürzig
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Ürzig” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Würzgarten, the spice garden, on red volcanic slate beneath the cliffs: the most exotic Mosel Riesling, spicy, tropical, firm.

study.name: Wiltingen
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Wiltingen” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Scharzhofberg is an Ortsteil, so the label reads Scharzhofberger without the village: grey slate on a south facing hill, among the most sought after Riesling vineyards in Germany. The Grosslage Wiltinger Scharzberg is a different thing.

study.name: Saarburg
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Saarburg” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Rausch, diabase and slate above the town, famous for Eiswein and Auslese.

study.name: Ruwer
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Ruwer” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: A small stream joining the Mosel just below Trier from the east; the vineyards sit in a side valley on slate with loam and give Riesling of great delicacy, herbs and blackcurrant leaf.

study.name: Zell
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Zell” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The town of the Grosslage Zeller Schwarze Katz, the black cat, a label the world drank by the million; its own single sites are better than the name.

study.name: Bremm
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Bremm” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Calmont, at up to 65 degrees counted the steepest vineyard in Europe, worked by monorack rail.

study.name: Winningen
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Winningen” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Near Koblenz: the Uhlen, bottled by its sub-soils, and the Röttgen on hard slate terraces; the lower Mosel's greatest dry Rieslings.

context.name: Steinbachweier

study.name: Lorch
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Lorch” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Beyond the bend, in the Mittelrhein gorge but legally Rheingau: slate, steep, Riesling late and lean; Bodental-Steinberg and Krone.

study.name: Assmannshausen
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Assmannshausen” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Where the river turns north: the Höllenberg, slate and phyllite, the home of Rheingau Spätburgunder for centuries and the state domaine's red cellar.

study.name: Rüdesheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Rüdesheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Rüdesheimer Berg, the steep western end on slate and quartzite above the river: Berg Schlossberg, the finest and driest, Berg Roseneck and Berg Rottland; Bischofsberg, Drachenstein and Klosterlay on gentler ground. Ripe even in cool years.

study.name: Geisenheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Geisenheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Rothenberg and Kläuserweg on loess tinged with slate, and the research and teaching institute of 1872 where Müller-Thurgau was bred; Johannisberg is one of its districts.

study.name: Johannisberg
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Johannisberg” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Schloss Johannisberg above the village, Benedictine from about 1100, planted to Riesling alone from 1720 and the birthplace of the Spätlese in 1775; the castle is an Ortsteil. Hölle and Klaus lie beside it.

study.name: Oestrich
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Oestrich” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Lenchen and Doosberg, broad sites near the river with the old wine crane on the bank: ripe, fruity Riesling and fine Auslese.

study.name: Kiedrich
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Kiedrich” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Set back from the river on phyllite and slate: the Gräfenberg, spicy and racy, among the finest Riesling and TBA sites in Germany; Turmberg and Wasseros beside it.

study.name: Rauenthal
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Rauenthal” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: High above Eltville, late ripening and spicy: Baiken, Gehrn, Rothenberg and Nonnenberg give Rieslings that need years.

study.name: Walluf
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Walluf” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The eastern village before Wiesbaden; the Walkenberg and old Riesling parcels.

study.name: Hochheim am Main
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Hochheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Apart on the Main east of Wiesbaden, on limestone and marl: Domdechaney, Kirchenstück, Hölle and Königin Victoriaberg, named for the queen's visit of 1845; rounder, earthier wines and the source of the word Hock.

context.name: Sporkenheim

context.name: Schierstein

study.name: Monzingen
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Monzingen” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Two classified sites face each other: the Halenberg, blue slate and quartzite, taut and smoky, and the Frühlingsplätzchen, red slate, fuller and more floral.

study.name: Meddersheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Meddersheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Rheingrafenberg, a south facing slope above the village: ripe, honeyed Spätlese that lives for decades.

study.name: Schloßböckelheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Schlossböckelheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Kupfergrube, the copper mine, cleared from 1902 by the Prussian state domaine on a worked out mine, porphyry on a steep south face: the most austere and longest lived dry Riesling of the valley; the Felsenberg, volcanic and steep, beside it, and the Königsfels.

study.name: Niederhausen
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Niederhausen” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Hermannshöhle, the Nahe's most complete site, porphyry and slate on a south face giving Riesling with everything; Hermannsberg, Klamm, Kertz and Steinberg beside it, and the old state domaine's buildings below.

study.name: Norheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Norheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Dellchen and Kirschheck, small volcanic sites of great finesse on the bend below Niederhausen.

study.name: Bockenau
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Bockenau” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: A side valley west of Bad Kreuznach: the Felseneck, slate and quartzite, taut, smoky and among the valley's best dry Riesling.

study.name: Bad Kreuznach
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Bad Kreuznach” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The spa town and the valley's capital: Kahlenberg, Krötenpfuhl and Brückes on sandstone and loess give rounder wines, and the trade has its base here.

study.name: Münster-Sarmsheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Münster-Sarmsheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Dautenpflänzer and Pittersberg, slate and quartzite near Bingen: firm, dry Riesling and good Pinot.

study.name: Langenlonsheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Langenlonsheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The warm end of the valley: Rothenberg and Löhrer Berg on loess and gravel.

study.name: Rüdesheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Rüdesheim an der Nahe” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The village behind the Rosengarten Grosslage; not the Rheingau's Rüdesheim, whatever the label suggests.

study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Nackenheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The northern end of the Roter Hang: the Rothenberg, red slate falling to the river, gives the Rhine's spiciest Riesling.

study.name: Oppenheim
study.lessonParent: Rheinterrasse and the Roter Hang (Bereich Nierstein)
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Oppenheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Sackträger and Kreuz on limestone and loess south of Nierstein, below the Katharinenkirche: rounder, riper Riesling.

study.name: Westhofen
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Westhofen” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Morstein, limestone over clay and the grandest of the Wonnegau; Kirchspiel, a south east facing bowl; Brunnenhäuschen and Aulerde: dry Riesling of weight and precision.

study.name: Hohen-Sülzen
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Hohen-Sülzen and Mölsheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Kirchenstück and the Zellerweg am Schwarzen Herrgott, limestone sites on the Pfalz border, dry and taut.

study.name: Mölsheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Hohen-Sülzen and Mölsheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Kirchenstück and the Zellerweg am Schwarzen Herrgott, limestone sites on the Pfalz border, dry and taut.

study.name: Worms
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Worms” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Liebfrauenkirche's own vineyard, the Liebfrauenstift-Kirchenstück, where Liebfraumilch began as a single wine before the name went generic across four regions.

study.name: Bingen am Rhein
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Bingen” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Scharlachberg, quartzite and slate on the Rochusberg above the Nahe's mouth, facing the Rheingau across the river: firm, mineral Riesling.

study.name: Ingelheim am Rhein
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Ingelheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The old red wine town, with Charlemagne's palace and Spätburgunder on limestone: the Pinot tradition of Rheinhessen.

study.name: Alzey
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Alzey” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The inland town at the centre of the triangle and the breeding station where Scheurebe was crossed in 1916.

study.name: Mainz
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Mainz” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The capital at the northern corner, the printing city, with the region's wine fairs and the Rhine's bend below it.

study.lessonNote: A handsome small town with limestone and sandstone sites such as Hohenmorgen, Kalkofen, Grainhübel and Langenmorgen, home to several historic estates. Its Riesling is a shade more elegant and floral than Forst's.

study.name: Bad Dürkheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Bad Dürkheim” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The spa town at the centre of the Mittelhaardt, with the Michelsberg and Spielberg sites and the Wurstmarkt, the enormous September wine festival.

study.name: Kallstadt
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Kallstadt” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: A limestone village north of Bad Dürkheim whose Saumagen vineyard, sharing its name with the stuffed pig's stomach dish of the Pfalz, gives chalky, long lived dry Riesling.

study.name: Königsbach
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Haardt, Gimmeldingen and Königsbach” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Villages above Neustadt with the Bürgergarten, Mandelgarten and Idig sites; the southern Mittelhaardt, where Riesling meets Scheurebe, Rieslaner and Spätburgunder.

study.name: Neustadt an der Weinstraße
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Neustadt an der Weinstrasse” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The region's wine capital at the join of the two Bereiche, with the research institute at Mussbach.

study.name: Laumersheim
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Laumersheim and the Zellertal” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The northern Pfalz towards Rheinhessen, on limestone and loess, where Spätburgunder and Riesling from Kirschgarten and the Schwarzer Herrgott have earned a modern reputation.

study.name: Birkweiler
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Birkweiler” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: A village west of Landau whose Kastanienbusch, on red slate, gives among the most mineral dry Riesling in the Pfalz; the Mandelberg is its limestone neighbour.

study.lessonNote: The coolest of the main villages, at the mouth of the Spitzer Graben: the Singerriedel and Hochrain terraces for Riesling, the Tausendeimerberg above the town, and the Honivogl site on deeper ground by the river for Grüner Veltliner.

study.name: Weißenkirchen in der Wachau
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Weissenkirchen” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The heart of Wachau Riesling: the Achleiten, a steep amphibolite and gneiss slope, the Klaus beside it and the Steinriegl above; Joching and Wösendorf are its neighbouring hamlets.

study.name: Dürnstein
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Dürnstein” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The postcard village under its ruined castle, where the Kellerberg rises in gneiss terraces that give the Wachau's most sought Riesling and Grüner Veltliner Smaragd; the Domäne Wachau cooperative has its cellars here.

study.name: Mautern
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Mautern” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: On the south bank opposite Stein, a Roman fort town; its vineyards on the gentler bank give a cooler, finer line of Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.

study.name: Krems an der Donau
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Krems and Stein” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The twin towns at the gorge's mouth: the Pfaffenberg and the Hund are gneiss terraces at Stein continuous with the Wachau's, giving Riesling of Wachau quality under a Kremstal label.

study.name: Senftenberg
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Senftenberg” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Up the Krems river north of the town, a steep gneiss gorge of its own: the Pellingen, Hochäcker and Piri terraces give tense, long lived Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.

study.name: Gedersdorf
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Rohrendorf and Gedersdorf” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The loess villages east of Krems, where Grüner Veltliner is broad and generous and Roter Veltliner appears; the Kremstal's bigger estates and the cooperative draw on these slopes.

study.name: Langenlois
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Langenlois” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The market town that gives the Kamptal its estates: the Käferberg, Steinmassl, Loiserberg, Spiegel and Dechant Rieden spread around it on loess, gneiss and gravel.

study.name: Zöbing
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Zöbing and the Heiligenstein” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Heiligenstein is a hill of Permian sandstone with volcanic grit, about 270 million years old, hot and bare, the Kamptal's Riesling summit; Ried Zöbinger Heiligenstein stands on the labels of the valley's best houses.

study.name: Kammern
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Kammern” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: Beneath the Heiligenstein: the Lamm, loess and clay at the hill's foot, is the Kamptal's finest Grüner Veltliner site, and the Grub, Renner and Gaisberg rise beside it.

study.lessonNote: The hill on the left bank of the Danube over Stammersdorf and Strebersdorf in the 21st district, loess over limestone and flysch: broad Grüner Veltliner, Weissburgunder and Riesling, and the city's largest block of vines; it continues into the Weinviertel beyond the city line.

study.name: Mauer

study.lessonNote: The southern vineyards of the 23rd district on the Maurer Berg at the foot of the Vienna Woods, brown earth and limestone, old mixed plantings with Zierfandler and Rotgipfler strands, and a quieter Heuriger scene.

study.lessonNote: The Laaer Berg in the 10th district, the city's south eastern slope on loess and gravel, warmer and drier, with Grüner Veltliner and reds.

study.lessonNote: Under the Manhartsberg against the Czech border: Retz with its famous cellar labyrinth beneath the town, Röschitz, Pulkau and Haugsdorf on granite, gneiss and loess, the driest and sunniest corner, Grüner Veltliner and a little Riesling.

study.name: Mailberg
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Mailberg” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: A sheltered basin south east of Retz, a warm pocket that makes the Weinviertel's best reds, Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch beside the Grüner Veltliner; the Knights of Malta have held an estate here since the twelfth century.

study.name: Poysdorf
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Poysdorf” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The northern Weinviertel's wine town, cool and late, long regarded as Austria's Sekt capital: Welschriesling and Grüner Veltliner for sparkling bases, Eiswein in cold years, and the Weinviertel DAC Reserve style from its loess slopes.

study.name: Falkenstein

study.lessonNote: Beneath a ruined castle on a Jurassic limestone cliff in the north, with Herrnbaumgarten and Staatz nearby: Grüner Veltliner with a chalky grip, among the region's most structured, and a classic Kellergasse.

study.name: Wolkersdorf im Weinviertel
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Wolkersdorf and the southern Weinviertel” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The warmest band, from the Bisamberg's northern slopes past Wolkersdorf and Stetten towards the Danube: riper Grüner Veltliner Reserve, Riesling on the Bisamberg's limestone and more red than the north.

study.name: Gols
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Gols” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The largest wine village of Burgenland on the lake's northern shore, home of the Pannobile growers and of the state's most ambitious reds, Zweigelt, Blaufränkisch and blends.

study.name: Frauenkirchen
study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Mönchhof, Frauenkirchen and Halbturn” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The villages behind the Seewinkel towards the Hungarian border, on gravel and loam, with reds and the sweet wines of estates that farm towards Illmitz.

study.name: Purbach am Neusiedler See

study.lessonNote: The slope villages of the west shore above the reeds, limestone and schist terraces for Leithaberg DAC Blaufränkisch and Weissburgunder, among the oldest vineyards of the lake.

study.name: Grosshöflein

study.name: Rust

study.name: Deutschkreutz

study.name: Leutschach

study.note: Town or settlement centre associated with “Kitzeck im Sausal” in the regional guide. The dot locates the settlement, not an appellation boundary or an individual vineyard.
study.lessonNote: The Sausal hills north of the border on schist and gneiss, with Kitzeck at about 560 metres among the highest wine villages in Europe: Riesling and Sauvignon Blanc with a slate edge, and the Ortswein name Kitzeck-Sausal.

study.name: Klöch
